items.title: 5 tiny habits for dark mornings
items.concept: A save-worthy list of five habits that each take under two minutes and make dark mornings easier. Positions the account as realistic rather than hustle.

script.headline: 1. Light **before** phone
script.body: Switch on a warm lamp before you touch your phone. Light tells your brain the day has started.

script.headline: 2. Water on the nightstand
script.body: Fill the glass the night before. Drink it before your feet touch the floor.

script.headline: 3. One song, not a playlist
script.body: Pick one song that means 'get up'. When it ends, you're up.

script.headline: 4. Open the curtains anyway
script.body: Even streetlight is light. It tells your body the night is over.

script.headline: 5. Decide breakfast **tonight**
script.body: One less decision at 7 a.m. is a calmer 7 a.m.

script.headline: Save this for **tomorrow** morning
script.body: Which one are you trying first? Comment 1-5.

items.caption:
Dark mornings aren't a discipline problem. They're a light problem.

Five tiny habits, each under 2 minutes:
1. Light before phone
2. Water on the nightstand
3. One song, not a playlist
4. Open the curtains, even in the dark
5. Decide breakfast the night before

Save this for tomorrow morning. Which one are you trying first? Comment 1-5.
items.creative_direction: Brand template: cover on deep green with terracotta emphasis, body slides on cream, recap slide as a numbered list. No photos needed. Keep every slide under 30 words.

items.title: 3 reasons your morning routine keeps failing
items.hook: Your morning routine isn't failing because you're lazy.
items.concept: Reframe failed routines as a design problem: copied from someone else, too long, and started too late (the night before). Edited from the raw talking-head footage of this week.

script.visual: Close-up, kitchen counter, morning light
script.voiceover: Your morning routine isn't failing because you're lazy.

script.visual: Punch-in
script.voiceover: Here are three reasons it keeps falling apart.

script.visual: Wide, then B-roll of an alarm at 05:00
script.voiceover: One: you copied someone else's routine. Start with one thing that already fits your actual morning.

script.visual: Punch-in
script.voiceover: Two: it's too long. Keep a ten-minute version for bad days.

script.visual: B-roll: phone face down on the nightstand
script.voiceover: Three: it starts the night before. Pick a phone-down time and protect it like a meeting.

script.visual: Back to close-up
script.voiceover: Make it yours, make it short, start the night before. Save this for tomorrow.

items.caption:
Your morning routine isn't failing because you're lazy.

It's failing because:
1. You copied someone else's
2. It's way too long
3. It starts at your alarm, not the night before

Save this for tomorrow morning, and tell me: which one is yours?
items.creative_direction: Talking head at the kitchen counter, phone at eye level, window light from the side. Cut with the AI Content Studio cut list: remove dead air, the retake of reason one and the 'um' before the hook. Alternate 100% / 112% punch-ins. Burned captions, lower-middle. items.title: 3 things I stopped doing before 9 a.m.
items.hook: I stopped doing these 3 things before 9 a.m. My mornings got quieter.
items.concept: A 'stop list' from personal experience: checking email in bed, reading the news, and planning the entire day. Relatable and shareable, about subtraction rather than adding habits.

script.visual: Phone screen with 37 unread emails, then the phone is turned face down
script.voiceover: I stopped doing these three things before 9 a.m.

script.visual: Bed, phone stays face down on the nightstand
script.voiceover: Checking email in bed. Nothing in there can't wait an hour.

script.visual: Radio or news app closed, kettle on
script.voiceover: Reading the news first thing. I read it at lunch now.

script.visual: A to-do list cut down to three lines
script.voiceover: Planning the entire day. I pick one thing that matters. The rest finds its place.

script.visual: Window, coffee, quiet
script.voiceover: Which one would you quit first?

items.caption:
Three things I stopped doing before 9 a.m.:

1. Checking email in bed
2. Reading the news
3. Planning the entire day

My mornings didn't get longer. They got quieter.

Which one would you quit first? Send this to the friend who checks email before brushing their teeth.
items.cta: Share it with a friend who needs it
items.creative_direction: Voice-over with slow, quiet B-roll in the bedroom and kitchen. Soft morning light, minimal props. Text pops on each number. Ends on a still shot to encourage a loop.
